name: Camera director
oneLiner: Replaces a hard-follow camera with a directed one: a critically damped spring with a dead zone, eased look-ahead in the facing or moving direction, vertical re-framing only on landing for side-scrollers, the hero and a boss kept in frame together (blended in by distance, zoom out without shrinking the hero, or a lean when the game cannot zoom), zoom punches and trauma shake (noise from game time, translation plus a small roll, capped) on big hits, level and room edges without jitter, and clean cuts on teleports. Sub-pixel for HD games, whole pixels for pixel games. View only: the game keeps its own camera for gameplay, so rules and autoplay endings never change.
fits: any scrolling game with a boss or a second player to frame
notFor: single-screen games with no scrolling (only the shake and punch would apply: use hit-stop-shake)
grid tactics whose camera jumps tile by tile on cursor moves (the cursor, not a hero, is the target)
games whose rules depend on exactly what is on screen and cannot keep their own camera for those checks
3D or WebGL scenes with their own camera

needs: a fixed update step that calls update(dt) once (also run by ?t= fast-forward and ?auto=1)
the followed target per step in world px: position, optional velocity, on-ground flag (side view) and facing
the level size (bounds); optional rooms or arenas
the world drawing wrapped by apply/restore (translate-style) or reading cam.x / cam.y (subtract-style); drawing culled with visible()
optional: extra targets to frame (boss, second player)
optional hit event: strength and contact point (hit), slams / explosions (trauma), teleports and respawns (cut)
optional: the game's own camera each step as legacy (mode off, tests)
optional: HUD and label rects (uiRects, screen px) the target must never be framed under
provides: the drawn camera: x, y, cx, cy, zoom, angle; apply / applyScreen / restore
visible() / inView() for draw culling; toScreen() / toWorld() for pointers and screen effects
trauma shake and zoom punch (hit, trauma, punch; shake(px, ms) for other elements' onShake)
cut() for teleports; auto cut on a target jump
debug(ctx) overlay (safe frame, dead zone, look-ahead, framing box, ground line, edges, trauma); stats() and state() for tests

params.label: Vertical band in the air (fraction of view height)
Camera above target (fraction of view height)
Smallest target on screen (fraction of view height)
Max trauma shake (% of view height)

assets: module/camera-director.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_Camera): exact critically damped springs, dead zone, look-ahead spring, platform snapping, multi-target framing with log-zoom spring, safe-frame catch-up, level clamp with zero speed, soft rooms, zoom punches, trauma shake from seeded value noise of game time, pixel snapping, debug overlay; the skin only sets the overlay accent and the pixel default
no image or audio files (the demo's level, hero, golem and backdrop are painted in code, original)

module.skin: optional: skins/skin-api.js + a skin before it (overlay accent, pixel snap default)
